Container.Name: Stellarr
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted text, voice and video chat for a group of friends. One container runs the web client, the API, object storage and the media server that carries every call.
On the Docker tab, open Logs from the container menu and copy the latest setup code. Choose WebUI from the same menu and enter the code to create the owner account and first server. Later accounts join through invite links. The owner's panel, Cockpit, is at /cockpit/.
On first start the container creates a self-signed certificate, so the browser shows a warning once. For a trusted certificate or a reverse proxy, see the documentation.
Container.Requires: Voice from other devices requires a reachable IPv4 address. Set Domain to that IPv4 address or set Public IP. For calls from outside your network, forward UDP and TCP port 49000 to the server on the same external port.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Database, uploads, encryption keys, generated secrets and TLS certificates. Keep it on a pool (cache) drive and back up the whole folder.

Config.Name: HTTPS port
Config.Description: The web client and Cockpit. Defaults to 8443 to avoid Unraid’s management port 443. Set HTTPS host port below to the same number.

Config.Name: Voice media port (UDP)
Config.Description: Preferred transport for voice and video. Use the same host port for UDP and TCP, set Voice media host port below to that number, and forward that port on the router.

Config.Name: Voice media port (TCP)
Config.Description: Fallback when UDP is unavailable. Use the same host port as UDP and forward TCP on that port on the router.

Config.Name: Domain
Config.Description: The name or IPv4 address people open Stellarr at, for example chat.example.com or 192.168.1.10. The certificate and public address use it. Empty means localhost, which only the Unraid server itself can use.

Config.Name: Dedicated activity domain (optional)
Config.Description: Leave empty to install activities from GitHub on this Stellarr address. A dedicated DNS suffix is optional. For example, enter activities.example.com here, point *.activities.example.com at Stellarr, and serve those hosts with a trusted wildcard certificate. If you use a reverse proxy, forward the wildcard hosts to the same Stellarr container. Keep the main Stellarr hostname outside this suffix.

Config.Name: Public IP
Config.Description: The IPv4 address browsers reach this server at: its LAN address for calls at home, your public address for calls over the internet, or auto to resolve the domain. If empty, an IPv4 address entered as Domain is used.

Config.Name: LAN IP for voice
Config.Description: Optional Unraid LAN IPv4 for people calling from the local network. Advertised alongside the public address on the voice media host port. Useful when the router does not loop traffic back through its public address.

Config.Name: HTTPS host port
Config.Description: The host side of the HTTPS port mapping above. The instance's public address uses it.

Config.Name: Voice media host port
Config.Description: The host side of the voice media port mapping above. The media server tells browsers this port.

Config.Name: Language
Config.Description: en or pl, English when empty: the web client's default language, and that of server messages, mail and the names of a new server's roles and channels.

Config.Name: Public HTTPS port
Config.Description: The HTTPS port browsers use, when it differs from the host port: 443 behind a reverse proxy. Empty means the HTTPS host port.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: The full address for mail links and desktop clients, for example https://chat.example.com. Overrides the address built from the domain and port.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: The reverse proxy in front of Stellarr, as the container sees it, for example 172.18.0.5: then each person's own address is recorded and rate-limited, not the proxy's. IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and networks, separated by commas. See the reverse proxy documentation for which address to list.

Config.Name: Explicit voice media addresses
Config.Description: Optional comma-separated IPv4 ip:port pairs for direct voice and video. Overrides the derived public, LAN and container addresses.

Config.Name: GIPHY key
Config.Description: Public GIPHY web key for GIF search. It can also be set in Cockpit under Integrations, which wins over this one.

Config.Name: Mail
Config.Description: true or false; true when empty. The first value of Cockpit's mail switch. The SMTP server, port and login are set in Cockpit.

Config.Name: SMTP password
Config.Description: Can also be set in Cockpit, which wins over this one.

Config.Name: Resend API key
Config.Description: Replaces SMTP when Resend is turned on in Cockpit under Integrations.

Config.Name: Mail sender name
Config.Description: Stellarr when empty.

Config.Name: OIDC sign-in
Config.Description: true or false; false when empty. Sign-in through an identity provider such as Pocket ID. Password sign-in stays available.

Config.Name: OIDC issuer
Config.Description: For example https://auth.example.com

Config.Name: OIDC button label
Config.Description: The label of the sign-in button; when empty, Main account, or Konto główne on a Polish instance.

Config.Name: Trust the provider's second step
Config.Description: true or false; false when empty. When true, a sign-in the provider confirmed with a second step counts as Stellarr's own.

Config.Name: Provider second-step amr values
Config.Description: The amr values that count as a second step when the setting above is true; mfa when empty.

Config.Name: Upload quota per user (bytes)
Config.Description: 2147483648 (2 GiB) when empty.

Config.Name: Upload quota in total (bytes)
Config.Description: 21474836480 (20 GiB) when empty.

Config.Name: Minimum free space (bytes)
Config.Description: Uploads are refused when the data folder has less free space than this; 1073741824 (1 GiB) when empty.

Config.Name: Concurrent uploads
Config.Description: 4 when empty.
